set.descent_text: The way down is fourth class with careful routefinding and should need no rappels, but it is easy to stray onto harder ground. From the summit, keep to the south end of the east face (climber's left of the ascent), downclimbing the blocky ridge back to the notch below Drizzlepuss. Climb back up to the top of Drizzlepuss, which is easier on its south side, then reverse the trail to the CMC campsite and carry on down the eroded trail to Leigh Lake and your canoe. A long vertical mile of descent separates the summit from the lake.
set.approach: Launch a canoe at String Lake, carry it over the short portage to Leigh Lake, and paddle across to the lake's far western corner, where Leigh Canyon opens out and campsite 14b sits. The overland route around the lakes is long, brushy and not maintained, which is why most parties paddle. From the shore below the East and West Horns, an obvious but eroded trail climbs the hillside for about 1,500 ft to the CMC campsite, traversing left just below it; follow cairns and tape on trees. From camp a trail leads up to the top of Drizzlepuss, with fourth class scrambling through the cliff bands, and a wrong turn puts you on fifth class ground. Descend from Drizzlepuss to the notch by downclimbing or a short rappel from an anchor north of the top; the east face climb starts in that notch.

review.notes: Route page and trip report agree on the canoe approach, the camp, Drizzlepuss and the notch, and on the 3rd/4th class no-rappel descent that reverses to the camp.

set.descent_text: The buttress ends in a bowl high on the south face, about a third of the way up the peak, and most parties descend from there. Many rappel from the east side of the bowl with double ropes, using trees and fixed anchors to reach the usual rappel line down the Blackfin chimneys and back to the ledges above Leigh Canyon. With a single rope you can instead follow the crest west to the end of the long horizontal section and take the couloirs that drop west toward the drainage between Moran and Thor Peak. To reach the summit instead, continue up the south ridge, or traverse east to join the CMC route and descend that. Early in the season an ice axe and crampons are useful.
set.approach: Launch a canoe at String Lake, carry it over the short portage to Leigh Lake, and paddle across to the lake's far western corner, where Leigh Canyon opens out and campsite 14b sits. The overland route around the lakes is long, brushy and not maintained, which is why most parties paddle. A faint climbers' path starts on the north side of the campsite and runs up Leigh Canyon, with cairns that split into several paths across the talus. Climb the scree and talus toward Laughing Lion Falls, then go up the lower ramp, passing a stand of trees and curving beneath the blunt arete of the buttress to a gully at its base. The line follows the prominent buttress rising from the left end of the higher of two ramps that slant across the face left of the falls; two approach pitches link the lower ramp to it.

review.notes: Approach and descent options agreed by the route page and trip report; rappel counts deliberately left out because the sources disagree.

The overland route around the lakes is long, brushy and not maintained, which is why most parties paddle. A faint climbers' path starts on the north side of the campsite and runs up Leigh Canyon, with cairns that split into several paths across the talus. The slabs lie below the large south face of No Escape Buttress, the first chunk of rock on the north side of Leigh Canyon. The easiest way to reach them is around from the west, though ledges allow a circuitous fourth class approach from the east.

review.notes: Slab position and access directions from the route page; canoe and campsite from the trip report. Descent skipped: no source gives one.

set.descent_text: The ridge meets the southeast ridge, where a large cairn marks a steep descent east back into Leigh Canyon. That descent is long, exposed and tedious, with consequential downclimbing, loose rock and scree, and a constant search for the easiest line to avoid rappels. The alternative is to follow the southeast ridge up toward Drizzlepuss and the CMC route, which adds hours but leads to the normal way down.
set.approach: Launch a canoe at String Lake, carry it over the short portage to Leigh Lake, and paddle across to the lake's far western corner, where Leigh Canyon opens out and campsite 14b sits. The overland route around the lakes is long, brushy and not maintained, which is why most parties paddle. A faint climbers' path starts on the north side of the campsite and runs up Leigh Canyon, with cairns that split into several paths across the talus. Approach up Leigh Canyon as for the other routes on the south buttress, then, close to the bottom of Laughing Lion Falls, walk uphill to a spring seeping from the wall on the east. Beyond it, exposed fourth class on dark stone leads to a break below the crest of the ridge, where the rope comes out.

review.notes: Single detailed route page; descent facts qualitative, with no counts. Canoe approach confirmed by the trip report.

set.descent_text: The last pitch ends on the sharp ridge of the buttress, and a fourth class scramble of a few hundred feet reaches the top of the buttress. From there, head north into the woods and follow a grassy drainage east toward Leigh Lake, bearing slightly right through thick vegetation in the lower part to return to campsite 14b. For a retreat from the lower pitches, rappel the line, noting that the second pitch is a steep overhang.
set.approach: Launch a canoe at String Lake, carry it over the short portage to Leigh Lake, and paddle across to the lake's far western corner, where Leigh Canyon opens out and campsite 14b sits. The overland route around the lakes is long, brushy and not maintained, which is why most parties paddle. From the campsite follow the climbers' trail west into Leigh Canyon to the large scree slope at the base of No Escape Buttress, the first rock wall in the canyon. The route starts about 250 ft left (west) of the pedestal start of the Direct South Face line, under the big arching roof.

review.notes: Route page for the finish and start position; walk-off from the West Arete page, which tops out on the same buttress.

set.descent_text: Walking off is easy. From the top of the buttress, head north into the woods and follow a grassy drainage east toward Leigh Lake. Lower down, bear slightly right through thick vegetation to arrive back at campsite 14b. No rappels are needed, and a single 60 m rope is enough for the climb.
set.approach: Launch a canoe at String Lake, carry it over the short portage to Leigh Lake, and paddle across to the lake's far western corner, where Leigh Canyon opens out and campsite 14b sits. The overland route around the lakes is long, brushy and not maintained, which is why most parties paddle. From the campsite a climbers' trail heads west up the canyon; after roughly half a mile a big scree fan spreads beneath the buttress. Angle up and left (west) to the toe of the West Arete, then climb a third class gully just west of the toe for a few hundred feet to the ledges below the splitter hand crack and roofs of the second pitch.

review.notes: Descent and approach from the route page; the Smoke and Mirrors page places the same buttress and top.

set.descent_text: The route reaches the crest near the notch beside Peak 11,795 and follows it to the north summit. The way back to camp is down the Northeast Ridge, a long and tiring descent that makes a clean round trip. Camp is placed as high as possible in the cirque below the ridge, so the descent returns there.
set.approach: Expect a rough approach day. Put in by boat at Spalding Bay and cross the water around the corner into Moran Bay, at the foot of the drainage coming off the ridge's north flank. From the shore comes severe bushwhacking up into the cirque beneath the ridge; camp as high as water allows. Above, continue toward the wide base of the ridge, pass right of a distinct darker buttress, then traverse left across its top on narrowing ledges until it is time to rope up.

review.notes: Single detailed route page; boat access to Moran Bay also implied by the Triple Glaciers page.

The overland route around the lakes is long, brushy and not maintained, which is why most parties paddle. A faint climbers' path starts on the north side of the campsite and runs up Leigh Canyon, with cairns that split into several paths across the talus. Follow Leigh Canyon up to the base of the south buttress, then leave the creek for the scree beside Laughing Lion Falls, as for South Buttress Right. The line starts in clean black-streaked corners about 25 m right of South Buttress Right, using the same access pitch.

review.notes: Position relative to South Buttress Right from the route page; shared approach from the SBR page and trip report. Descent skipped: the route page does not say where it ends.

wy_south_buttress_prow.skip_reason: Route page gives only a one-line location with contradictory directions relative to neighbouring lines; no top-out or approach detail.

set.descent_text: Descent is by rappel. From the top, the first anchors lead right toward the head of Laughing Lion Falls, then right again at the break col to a large ledge whose anchors are hidden to the hard left. Below that, find the large steep gully on the right, which funnels the rappel line toward the ledge where the route began. The last rappel is on the far east end of that ledge, bringing you back to the spot where gear is usually stashed. Take two ropes; most stations are bolts or well slung.
set.approach: Launch a canoe at String Lake, carry it over the short portage to Leigh Lake, and paddle across to the lake's far western corner, where Leigh Canyon opens out and campsite 14b sits. The overland route around the lakes is long, brushy and not maintained, which is why most parties paddle. A faint climbers' path starts on the north side of the campsite and runs up Leigh Canyon, with cairns that split into several paths across the talus. Keep near the creek bed until you can make out the two large ledge systems angling west on your right at the bottom of the south buttress. Directly below them, turn right and climb the scree until you are level with the foot of Laughing Lion Falls, a good place to stash gear. Scramble the first ledge and fourth class ground to the second ledge, where the route starts.

review.notes: Descent and approach from the route page; DSB page and trip report confirm shared rappel line and the canoe approach. Rappel count left out.

set.descent_text: The couloir is also used as the way down, and in spring it can be the easiest way up and down the peak. Descend the same couloir, using a short rope around the fifth class chockstone near the top. Stay watchful for avalanche: when the sun or a storm hits it, the long, partly channelled couloir slides. Crampons and an ice tool are standard in snowy conditions.
set.approach: From the campsite at the Leigh Lake inlet, follow the climbers' and game trail beside the bear box. Hike beneath the south face and the Sandinista Couloir, staying in the gullies about 200 m out from the wall, to reach the foot of the couloir. Early in the season the snow is flat and white before mid May.

review.notes: Single route page; shared top with the Triple Glaciers line from both pages.

wy_triple_glaciers_nnw_face.skip_reason: Route page is a mood description with no top-out, descent or approach line; boat access only. Not enough to write from.
